audits.registerSummary: Ranger-General reading streets as ground: chokepoints, sightlines, blind lanes, gait (drilled against tired), who watches whom. Her inner voice argues in short turns: a question, a bad answer, an overrule, ending in an action ('Leave it in the wall. Take the man.'). It is dry and unfair to slow humans, and she knows it. She names no feelings and reads bodies before social meaning. She would not reach for lyrical cadence, thematic summary, or atmosphere for its own sake.

The A7 'a man who / anyone' generalizations (L25, L63, L159, L243, L277, L325, L341) each feed a decision. The A8 sound and smell lines (L337, L341, L347) name their source first. The one A1-shaped fragment that restates (L405) is filed under F4 in the gpt-5 guide. The tool's one pass-B hit (verdict_enough_for, L223) is a concrete dimension and was kept.

audits.cleanReason: 15 candidates were examined (L153, L159, L195, L199, L201, L209, L261, L321 tally, L365, L381, L391, L431, L437, L439, L451). Each one cashes out from the page. The split-task paragraph at L195 names the door (a magister's ring), the bags, the lane and the gait problem, which makes it the anchored counterpart of the guide's 'She had the street shape' example. The tactical inferences (L261, L321 tally, L381) follow evidence shown at L255, L259 and L317-L319. Jaina's 'What it carries only wakes once the bread's eaten' (L365) is an operational distinction held to the plan's resolution (carrier layer applied at packaging, the body finishes the work). Abstract dialogue words ('properly' L391, 'the city's theirs' L431, 'his death sewn into his collar' L439) are cashed out in the same speech or by L257. The keep rate is above the guide's 25% warning because four revision rounds have already removed the stand-ins. The same nouns were checked for repeats: none.

The chapter has no explicit translation setup ('plainly', 'say it in streets', 'short version'). The four nearest exchanges were audited as exchanges. 'Where are people sick, Captain?' (L99-L101) gets the mill lane from the weir bridge to the Corn Exchange, four named yards, the bakers at the bottom of the lane and a symptom course. 'Is it?' (L103-L105) gets a usable threshold: the widow on this corner against her sister across the way, who buy from different ovens. Jaina's account to non-mages (L365) gives when (after dressing, before sewing), how (by hand, worked through) and the limit ('It doesn't tell me whose hands'). Corin's 'They'll be gone by then' (L393-L397) gives Kett's bills, the first carts out, the south and weir roads, and a trigger ('before your clerk has his boots on'). None needs a second unpacking.
